chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from one who narrated to him, from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no matter regarding which two (people) differ except that it has an origin in the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic — but the intellects of men do not reach it.'

key_terms.أَصْل: Origin, root, foundational principle — that every ruling or answer is traceable to a Quranic basis
key_terms.أَمْر: Matter, affair, dispute — here referring to any point of doctrinal or legal disagreement
key_terms.عُقُولُ الرِّجَالِ: The intellects of men — ordinary human reason, as distinct from the divinely guided intellect of the Imams
key_terms.كِتَابُ اللَّهِ: The Book of God (the Quran) — presented as the ultimate comprehensive authority

ai.seo_question: Does the Quran contain the origin of every disputed matter according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) asserts that every disputed matter has its resolution in the Quran, though human intellect is limited and cannot always access those answers. This teaching is part of al-Kulayni's chapter on the comprehensive authority of the Quran and Sunnah, emphasizing that divine revelation covers all of human need — but that full comprehension requires the guidance of those (the Imams) whose intellects are capable of plumbing its depths. The hadith was transmitted through al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, a devoted companion of the Imam who was later martyred for his loyalty.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from the one who narrated it, from Al Moalla Bin Khunays who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is none from a matter regarding which two (people) differ except for it would have its origin in the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, but the intellects of the men do not reach it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Al-Thaqafi‘laba ibn Maymun from one he narrated from al-Mu‘alla ibn Khunays who has said the following.

“Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) has said, ‘There is no issue which would be disputed between two people but that there is a principle for it the book of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, only the man’s power of Intelligence is not able to reach it.’”
